headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, like data centers, to pay for their increased grid capacity costs, preventing these expenses from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Senator Mark Warner, Governor Abigail Spanberger, Dominion Energy.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_summary: House Bill 1393 requires the State Corporation Commission to separate utility infrastructure costs, ensuring data centers drawing 25 megawatts or more pay for their grid expansions. This prevents transmission fee costs from spiking residential bills, a measure supported by Senate Majority Leader Scott Surovell to ensure data centers pay their fair share.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates local water authorities to publicly report data centers' water usage, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide credible data for public access and water supply planning, addressing concerns about the industry's significant water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for large data centers, requiring sound assessments near homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, environmental groups, local government planning departments, Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Scott Surovell.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry, economic development agencies.
news_headline: Data Center Siting Restrictions Gain Traction
news_summary: Virginia passed new data center siting restrictions, including HB 153, which establishes a permit process for facilities using 100 MW or more. The bill requires sound assessments near homes and schools within 500 feet and allows localities to assess impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites before approving projects.
